column1: # slug|impact,uniqueness,significance,experience,depth|category overrides or -|individual rationale
sanxingdui-museum|9.5,9.7,9.8,9.5,9.2|-|Remarkable Bronze Age assemblages justify elite uniqueness, but one museum's visitor reach need not exceed the Forbidden City.

dujiangyan-irrigation-system|9.1,9.6,9.8,9.0,8.6|-|Exceptional ancient engineering system with worldwide impact; an infrastructure visit is less immediately immersive than large heritage palace ensembles.
leshan-giant-buddha|9.2,9.7,9.7,9.2,8.1|-|Immense singular carved Buddha with rich history, but one monument has narrower depth than a comprehensive pilgrimage complex.
victoria-harbour|9.3,9.3,8.8,9.6,9.0|-|Extraordinary city/harbour panorama, yet skyline scenery is not equivalent to unique ancient archaeological significance.
xian-city-wall|9.1,9.4,9.6,9.2,8.8|-|Exceptional complete urban fortifications with traversable perimeter, below Great Wall stretches in global singularity.
historic-centre-macau|9.1,9.4,9.5,9.1,9.2|-|Important Sino-Portuguese urban fabric with multiple monuments; heritage significance should be below world-defining imperial sites.
mount-everest-north-base-camp|9.6,9.5,9.1,8.7,8.0|-|World's highest mountain gives immense visual impact, but base-camp stop is not equivalent to climbing Everest or exploring the massif.
mount-kailash|9.6,9.8,9.7,8.8,8.5|-|Globally significant sacred mountain and pilgrimage landscape, with experience and depth separate from the summit and whole region.
gulangyu-island|9.2,9.2,9.0,9.2,9.0|-|Distinctive historic island with layered architecture but not as globally consequential as top UNESCO urban ensembles.
fujian-tulou-yongding|9.5,9.6,9.5,9.3,9.0|-|Rare communal earthen buildings and living heritage; group visitor breadth below citywide historic ensembles.
dazu-rock-carvings|9.5,9.7,9.8,9.3,8.9|-|Exceptionally important dispersed Buddhist carvings, though travel between components changes visitor depth from a single museum.
wudang-mountains|9.4,9.6,9.7,9.3,9.1|-|Exceptional Daoist sacred landscape with historic monasteries, but not every field needs near-perfect score.
stone-forest-shilin|9.2,9.4,8.9,9.3,8.6|-|Exceptional limestone formations with scenic depth, but world-geology significance is below iconic reference sites such as Huangshan.
temple-of-heaven|9.5,9.6,9.8,9.5,9.1|-|Extraordinary imperial ritual park, yet slightly less singular than the Forbidden City complex.
great-wall-jiankou|9.5,9.6,9.4,9.0,8.3|-|Dramatic wild Great Wall stretch, but difficult, fragmented visitor experience and scale differ from Jinshanling.
pingyao-ancient-city|9.1,9.4,9.6,9.2,9.1|-|Exceptionally preserved historic trading city, with much stronger urban breadth than a single city gate.
zhangye-danxia|9.4,9.7,8.9,9.5,8.6|-|Extraordinary colored hills and geology but controlled scenic stops have narrower depth than huge protected landscapes.

badain-jaran-desert|9.4,9.7,9.0,9.3,9.1|-|Keep rare mega-dune and interdunal-lake landscape, newly UNESCO-inscribed and internationally exceptional in geomorphology; slightly moderate experience and depth relative to a fully visitable multi-site landscape. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1638/

forbidden-city|9.9,9.9,10.0,9.8,9.5|-|Retain exact approved worldwide significance ten: Ming-Qing imperial palace preserves unparalleled ensemble architectural layout and cultural history, unlike smaller palace or ceremonial complexes. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/439

great-wall-jinshanling|10.0,10.0,10.0,9.8,9.2|-|Retain exact registered ten anchors for engineering impact, uniqueness and global heritage: exceptional preserved and hikeable Ming wall system at a prime Great Wall section. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/438

great-wall-mutianyu|9.8,9.8,9.9,9.7,9.0|-|Retain extraordinary, coherent, frequently visited Great Wall mountain-fortification section, though less singular in adventure and scale than the designated Jinshanling reference. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/438

huanglong-scenic-area|9.5,9.7,9.1,9.6,9.1|-|Retain globally unusual travertine pools, waterfalls and forest mountain setting, geographically and scientifically separate from Jiuzhaigou rather than a generic mountain viewpoint. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/638

jiuzhaigou-valley|9.8,9.7,9.4,9.8,9.1|-|Retain exceptional lakes, waterfalls and alpine forest recognized internationally as a globally defining protected landscape; existing category nature ten remains an approved anchor. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/637

jokhang-temple|9.3,9.8,9.9,9.2,8.6|-|Retain centuries of Tibetan Buddhist religious centrality with meaningful architecture and pilgrim tradition, a discrete component of the Potala UNESCO ensemble rather than a substitute for the whole city. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/707

kanas-lake|8.8,9.0,8.4,8.9,8.4|nature=9.1|Scenic glacial alpine lake and forests but international comparisons with Jiuzhaigou and large lake systems do not support extraordinary uniqueness or world-class category nature 9.5 for the lake alone. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/637

kashgar-old-city|8.8,8.8,8.7,8.9,8.6|architecture=8.8,culture=9.1|Exceptionally significant Silk Road and living Uyghur urban identity, but substantial demolition and tourism-oriented rebuilding reduce authenticity of the built historic fabric; cannot equate the present old-city streets with an intact medieval UNESCO city. Source: https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0016718521003328

li-river-guilin|9.7,9.8,9.1,9.7,9.2|-|Retain globally exceptional navigable karst river-landscape and iconic limestone towers; compare against Ha Long Bay's partly submerged tower-karst rather than a local riverboat outing. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/statesparties/cn

longmen-grottoes|9.7,9.9,9.9,9.6,9.2|-|Retain vast cliff-carved sculptural gallery with thousands of niches and internationally influential Buddhist art, not comparable to one standalone cave shrine. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1003

mogao-caves|9.8,9.9,9.9,9.5,9.4|-|Retain exceptional 492-site cave sanctuary heritage and a millennium of Buddhist murals and sculpture, far broader and more consequential than an ordinary visitor cave. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/440

mount-huangshan|9.9,9.9,9.6,9.8,9.3|-|Retain approved world-defining nature and photography category anchors for extraordinary granite peaks, cloudscapes and landscape-cultural influence. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/statesparties/cn

potala-palace|9.8,9.9,9.9,9.4,9.2|-|Retain emblematic Tibetan religious and royal architectural complex at Lhasa with extraordinary historical and artistic significance; Jokhang remains individually scored, not copied into palace depth. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/707

summer-palace|9.5,9.7,9.7,9.5,9.2|-|Beijing's exceptionally extensive imperial garden landscape is globally distinguished, but historical singularity and scope should remain slightly below the capital's Forbidden City palace nucleus. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/880/

terracotta-army|9.9,10.0,10.0,9.7,9.1|-|Retain exact approved uniqueness and significance tens for Qin imperial life-size army and world-defining funerary archaeological assemblage; the pit museum is narrower in visit depth than full mausoleum region. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/441

yungang-grottoes|9.6,9.9,9.9,9.6,9.0|-|Retain exceptional 5th-6th century carved Buddhist caves and mature sculptural styles, with global comparison to Mogao and Longmen rather than small local rock shrines. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/statesparties/cn

zhangjiajie-national-forest-park|9.8,9.7,9.3,9.8,9.3|-|Retain iconic forest of sandstone pinnacles with extraordinary visual experience and park-level multi-trail discovery; geological landforms supported within UNESCO Wulingyuan. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/640

wulingyuan-scenic-area|9.6,9.7,9.3,9.5,9.6|nature=9.8,photography=9.7|The UNESCO-listed Wulingyuan landscape includes globally unusual quartz-sandstone pillars and extensive scenic valleys; an entire protected landscape should not remain at five identical provisional 8.5 fields while its nested Zhangjiajie forest park is scored 96.25. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/statesparties/cn

mount-emei|9.4,9.5,9.8,9.3,9.5|nature=9.5,history=9.8,culture=9.7|UNESCO mixed heritage recognizes an exceptional sacred Buddhist mountain with centuries of temples, forests and varied pilgrim routes; five identical 8.5 fields badly understate global cultural and landscape significance. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/statesparties/cn

fanjing-mountain|9.3,9.5,9.1,9.0,9.1|nature=9.8,history=8.9|UNESCO Fanjingshan has rare subtropical ecological communities, notable endemic and threatened plants and mountain habitats; exceptional natural uniqueness merits substantially higher scores than generic 8.5, without claiming a perfect visitor experience. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/statesparties/cn

yuanyang-rice-terraces|9.2,9.5,9.4,9.3,9.4|nature=9.5,history=9.6|Honghe Hani terrace systems are a UNESCO cultural landscape of enduring water management, village and agricultural traditions; a multi-valley working heritage site has rare cultural depth versus ordinary scenic rice fields. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/statesparties/cn

pu-er-jingmai-tea-forests|8.9,9.4,9.3,9.2,9.1|nature=9.3,history=9.5|Jingmai Mountain old-tea-forest landscape is a 2023 UNESCO cultural heritage property with traditional forest management and connected villages; it is more historically singular than an ordinary tea plantation but less visually defining than Huangshan. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/statesparties/cn

wuyi-mountains|9.4,9.5,9.4,9.4,9.5|nature=9.8,history=9.5,culture=9.4,photography=9.5|UNESCO mixed designation covers distinctive Danxia river gorges, biodiversity, tea growing and long scholarly heritage; whole protected mountain range's breadth is much greater than flat baseline 8.5 suggested. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/statesparties/cn

mount-tai|9.4,9.6,9.8,9.2,9.4|nature=9.3,history=9.9,culture=9.9|Mount Taishan's globally consequential Chinese imperial rites and sacred pilgrimage routes justify elite cultural significance but its scenic and visitor experience need not inherit Huangshan's landscape reference tens. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/statesparties/cn

wutaishan-mountain|9.1,9.5,9.7,9.3,9.5|history=9.8,culture=9.8,architecture=9.7|UNESCO Mount Wutai is a large historic Buddhist religious landscape with monasteries over a broad mountainous region, not simply a single temple; significant international Buddhist influence and exploration depth merit uplift. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/statesparties/cn

sanqingshan-mountain|9.4,9.5,9.1,9.4,9.2|nature=9.8,photography=9.7|UNESCO Mount Sanqingshan is recognized for extraordinary granite pinnacles, cliffs and changing cloudscapes; site-wide alpine landscape merits exceptional natural photographic scoring beyond undifferentiated 8.5 fields. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/statesparties/cn

lijiang-old-town|9.3,9.5,9.5,9.3,9.5|architecture=9.7,history=9.6|UNESCO Old Town of Lijiang preserves a distinctive Naxi-influenced historic urban layout, canals and many traditional buildings; assess city-scale streets as a coherent site, above a generic local town but below the biggest imperial city. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/statesparties/cn

west-lake-hangzhou|9.1,9.4,9.5,9.4,9.5|nature=9.2,history=9.7,culture=9.6,photography=9.4|West Lake UNESCO cultural landscape inspired historic Chinese garden and landscape traditions across East Asia; broad causeways, pavilions and scenic routes justify exploration depth and significance beyond a single urban lake. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/statesparties/cn

beijing-central-axis|9.0,9.3,9.4,9.2,9.5|architecture=9.5,history=9.6,culture=9.4|The 2024 UNESCO Beijing Central Axis is a 7.8-km urban planning ensemble connecting monumental imperial spaces, with more historic and physical breadth than any single tower, gate or short street segment. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/statesparties/cn

western-xia-tombs|8.9,9.4,9.5,9.0,8.8|history=9.7,architecture=9.1|The 2025 UNESCO-inscribed Xixia imperial tomb landscape includes significant royal funerary archaeology and distinctive earthen monuments, while the visitor experience is not as comprehensive as a restored imperial palace. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/statesparties/cn

yinxu-ruins|9.1,9.5,9.8,8.9,9.0|history=9.9,culture=9.6|Yin Xu is UNESCO-listed Shang dynasty capital archaeological heritage associated with oracle-bone writing and early urban civilization; historic significance approaches world-defining despite partially exposed excavated remains. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/statesparties/cn

mount-lushan|9.1,9.3,9.4,9.1,9.4|nature=9.3,history=9.6,culture=9.5|Lushan UNESCO cultural landscape combines forested mountains and celebrated temples and art traditions inspiring Chinese landscape aesthetics; the coherent mountain landscape offers multiple exploration routes. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/statesparties/cn

kekexili-honoh-xil|9.2,9.6,9.6,8.4,9.2|nature=9.8,wildlife=9.8|Qinghai Hoh Xil UNESCO natural property safeguards globally exceptional high-altitude Tibetan Plateau ecosystems and seasonal antelope migration; outstanding ecology is not equivalent to accessible mainstream tourist experience. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/statesparties/cn

mount-qingcheng|9.0,9.2,9.5,9.1,9.2|nature=9.2,history=9.7,culture=9.7|Mount Qingcheng in the UNESCO Dujiangyan mixed cultural listing is a key Daoist sacred mountain with temples along scenic forest trails; stronger historic and pilgrimage uniqueness than a generic wooded hill. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/statesparties/cn

confucius-temple-qufu|9.1,9.5,9.8,9.2,8.9|architecture=9.6,history=9.9,culture=9.9|Qufu UNESCO temple and cemetery ensemble marks the birthplace and enduring global cultural influence of Confucianism; a historically transformative heritage site with less physical tour depth than a whole capital. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/statesparties/cn

humble-administrators-garden|9.0,9.4,9.3,9.3,8.5|architecture=9.6,history=9.5,nature=9.1,photography=9.3|The Humble Administrator's Garden is a leading component of UNESCO Classical Gardens of Suzhou, a reference example of literati garden design; concentrated gardens offer less depth than a full district. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/statesparties/cn

kaiping-diaolou|9.0,9.4,9.1,9.1,9.0|architecture=9.8,history=9.2,culture=9.3|UNESCO Kaiping Diaolou comprises unusual fortified multi-story houses and villages reflecting overseas Chinese cultural exchange; broader architectural heritage deserves a higher unique global comparison than boilerplate 8.5. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/statesparties/cn

shenyang-imperial-palace|9.0,9.2,9.2,9.0,8.8|architecture=9.4,history=9.5,culture=9.2|Shenyang palace is part of the UNESCO Ming-Qing Imperial Palaces property, historically distinctive earlier Manchu court architecture but smaller and less singular than Beijing's Forbidden City. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/statesparties/cn

zuojiang-huashan-rock-art|9.1,9.6,9.4,8.6,8.4|history=9.7,culture=9.6|UNESCO Zuojiang Huashan rock art is a rare extensive cliff painting ensemble connected to ancient Luoyue rituals, with outstanding painted cultural heritage but narrower visitor access and interpretive depth. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/statesparties/cn

wulong-karst|9.2,9.5,9.1,9.2,9.0|nature=9.8,adventure=9.1|UNESCO South China Karst includes remarkable Wulong natural bridges, sinkholes and gorge geomorphology, internationally distinctive even as a component of the wider multi-site karst World Heritage property. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/statesparties/cn

maijishan-grottoes|9.3,9.7,9.6,9.2,8.9|architecture=9.8,history=9.8,culture=9.7|Maijishan cliffside Buddhist grottoes are part of the Silk Roads UNESCO serial heritage and an outstanding sculptural tradition, visited within a concentrated but unusually large cliff cave ensemble. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/statesparties/cn

kizil-caves|9.1,9.6,9.5,8.9,8.7|history=9.8,architecture=9.5,culture=9.6|Kizil is an early Buddhist cave-painting sanctuary on the UNESCO Silk Roads heritage corridor; historical originality is globally high but restricted access and surviving murals limit direct visitor breadth. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/statesparties/cn

jiaohe-ruins|9.0,9.4,9.2,9.0,8.8|history=9.6,architecture=9.3|The earthen Jiaohe ancient city ruins form part of the UNESCO Silk Roads Chang'an-Tianshan network; extraordinary preserved street and building layout gives substantial real on-site depth. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/statesparties/cn

norbulingka-palace|8.8,9.0,9.2,9.0,8.7|architecture=9.2,history=9.3|Norbulingka's landscaped summer palace and Tibetan religious-political heritage belong to the UNESCO Potala ensemble, but the compact palace does not merit every dimension at massive Potala Palace scale. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/statesparties/cn

baodingshan-carvings|9.2,9.6,9.4,9.1,8.6|history=9.7,architecture=9.7|Baodingshan rock carvings are a key magnificent component of the UNESCO Dazu Rock Carvings site; assess the one sculpted hillside rather than awarding the full multi-site heritage group's depth. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/statesparties/cn

songshan-mountain|9.0,9.2,9.3,9.1,9.2|nature=9.1,history=9.6,culture=9.5|Mount Song's historically influential Chinese sacred-mountain cultural landscape surrounds UNESCO Dengfeng monuments, but the mountain region's uniqueness should not be copied from the world-leading Shaolin temple name alone. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/statesparties/cn

qinghai-lake|9.2,9.2,8.9,9.0,9.0|nature=9.5,wildlife=9.1|Qinghai Lake is China's largest inland saline lake and a major high-altitude bird-breeding wetland. Its extraordinary plateau ecosystem merits higher nature and significance than an ordinary scenic lake, but not near-perfect visitor depth. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/tentativelists/6186/

harbin-ice-snow-world|9.2,9.4,8.4,9.5,9.1|architecture=9.5,photography=9.5|Harbin's seasonal Ice and Snow World is among the largest purpose-built winter attractions with giant sculpted ice architecture, but its ephemeral event does not have the centuries-deep significance of an ancient city. Source: https://english.www.gov.cn/news/202502/26/content_WS67bf0a0cc6d0868f4e8effd2.html

hongyadong|8.3,8.1,7.2,8.8,8.0|architecture=8.9,photography=9.1|Chongqing's photogenic eleven-floor stilt-house-style retail complex opened in 2006 as new construction rather than preserved ancient dwellings; strong skyline appeal should not be mistaken for original historical architecture. Source: https://english.cq.gov.cn/specials/explore/PhotoPerfectSpots/202608/t20260810_15912600.html

changbai-mountain|9.4,9.4,9.1,9.2,9.2|nature=9.7,photography=9.4|Changbaishan is a UNESCO Global Geopark and Biosphere Reserve with stratovolcano, crater lake, alpine habitats and hot springs; mountain-wide ecosystem and volcanic science exceed a single lake viewpoint's scope. Source: https://www.unesco.org/en/iggp/mount-changbaishan-unesco-global-geopark

heaven-lake-changbai|9.1,9.3,8.8,9.1,8.1|nature=9.5,photography=9.5|Tianchi is a spectacular high volcanic crater lake at Changbaishan summit, but a usually short weather-dependent lake viewpoint should not carry the entire mountain protected reserve's visitor depth. Source: https://www.unesco.org/en/iggp/mount-changbaishan-unesco-global-geopark

heavenly-lake-tianshan|8.8,8.9,8.5,8.9,8.0|nature=9.2,photography=9.2|Heavenly Lake near Bogda Peak combines accessible water and steep Tianshan forest scenery, but the specific lake is one small component of the larger UNESCO Xinjiang Tianshan mountains. Source: https://english.igsnrr.cas.cn/ecg/naturalscenery/lakes/202011/t20201119_251400.html

labrang-monastery|9.2,9.4,9.6,9.1,9.0|architecture=9.5,history=9.6,culture=9.7|Labrang is one of the six major Gelug Tibetan monasteries, with monastic colleges, sacred art and active pilgrim tradition, providing much more cultural depth than generic 8.5 but less empire-wide scale than the Jokhang-Potala core. Source: https://www.lonelyplanet.com/points-of-interest/labrang-monastery/1239039

lake-manasarovar|9.2,9.5,9.7,8.8,8.6|nature=9.4,culture=9.8|Manasarovar is a sacred high-altitude Tibetan Plateau lake in Hindu, Buddhist, Bon and Jain pilgrimage, giving exceptional cross-religious cultural importance, even if the lake shore visit is less varied than Kailash region-wide trekking. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/tentativelists/6187/

mausoleum-qin-shi-huang|9.3,9.7,9.9,8.3,8.5|history=9.9,culture=9.8|The immense First Emperor's burial landscape is globally consequential Qin history, but the sealed central mausoleum mound is a different visitor attraction from the Terracotta Army pits and should not inherit their museum experience. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/441

meili-snow-mountains|9.4,9.5,9.1,9.0,9.1|nature=9.7,photography=9.6|Meili is an extensive sacred glaciated range within the UNESCO Three Parallel Rivers landscape, with severe peaks and Tibetan pilgrimage importance; mountain scenery is profound, but ordinary direct summit visitation is not accessible. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/document/117331

mount-huashan|9.4,9.5,9.6,9.4,8.9|nature=9.5,history=9.7,adventure=9.6|Huashan is one of China's Five Great sacred mountains with dramatic near-vertical granite hiking routes and religious heritage; legitimate multi-route mountain visit, though no claim that it is already UNESCO-inscribed. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/tentativelists/1626/

pamir-highway-china|9.0,9.1,8.6,9.1,9.2|nature=9.5,adventure=9.2|The Chinese Karakoram Highway is a major multi-day mountain route traversing the Pamirs via Tashkurgan and Khunjerab toward Pakistan, but score the road experience rather than the entire Pamir mountain ecosystem. Source: https://www.xinjiangattractions.com/china-pakistan-highway-guide-the-ultimate-road-trip/

shaanxi-history-museum|9.3,9.5,9.7,9.5,9.4|history=9.8,culture=9.7|Shaanxi History Museum states its holdings include about 1.7 million objects from historic Chinese capital regions including Han and Tang; national collection depth strongly exceeds a generic local museum, but is below the largest global imperial collections. Source: https://en.sxhm.com/en/new/about.html

longji-rice-terraces|9.0,9.1,8.8,9.3,9.0|nature=9.3,culture=9.3,photography=9.5|Longji's large traditional Zhuang and Yao working terraces date across centuries, offering mountain hikes and settlement experiences, but should not be confused with the separate UNESCO Honghe Hani rice terrace landscape. Source: https://visitguilin.org/things-to-do/longsheng-attractions/longji-rice-terraces/

yading-nature-reserve|9.5,9.5,9.1,9.2,9.5|nature=9.8,photography=9.6|UNESCO MAB Yading covers rare alpine valleys, sacred snow peaks, glaciers and exceptionally rich high mountain forest biodiversity; meaningful multi-day trekking warrants far greater depth than a flat 8.5 profile. Source: https://www.unesco.org/en/mab/yading

shaolin-temple|9.4,9.5,9.8,9.3,8.9|history=9.9,culture=9.9|Shaolin Temple is globally consequential for Chan Buddhism and martial arts history and forms part of the UNESCO Dengfeng historic monuments; its compact core and pagoda forest remain less extensive than full imperial archaeological sites. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1305

jiayuguan-fort|9.1,9.4,9.5,9.0,8.5|architecture=9.6,history=9.7|Jiayuguan Pass is the monumental western Ming fortress and terminus of the Great Wall in arid Gansu, distinguished from the hundreds-of-kilometres wall experience and from a generic small castle. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/pg.cfm?CID=31&ID_SITE=438&l=EN

tashilhunpo-monastery|9.2,9.3,9.4,9.0,9.0|architecture=9.5,history=9.7|Tashilhunpo is a large 15th-century active Tibetan monastery associated with the Panchen Lama, with substantial chapels and monastic grounds, though not equal globally to Potala Palace's historical role. Source: https://cnto.org.au/tibet/

turpan-karez-system|8.9,9.3,9.4,8.5,8.1|history=9.6,architecture=9.2|Turpan's ancient subterranean gravity-fed karez irrigation network is rare engineering heritage that sustained desert settlements, but tourist exhibits expose only a limited part of the entire functioning water system. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/tentativelists/5347/

samye-monastery|9.3,9.5,9.8,9.2,9.1|-|Samye is traditionally regarded as Tibet's first Buddhist monastery with distinctive mandala-inspired layout, enormously important Tibetan religious heritage yet less museum-style depth than a large imperial palace.

gongga-mountain|9.3,9.5,8.9,8.9,9.1|-|Mount Gongga (Minya Konka) is an immense glaciated Sichuan peak and mountaineering landmark with profound mountain scale, but direct summit access is exceptionally demanding.

taklamakan-desert|9.5,9.5,9.2,8.6,9.7|-|The vast Taklamakan is one of the world's largest shifting sand deserts and a defining Silk Road barrier, globally significant wilderness but a challenging rather than convenient visit.

bingling-temple-grottoes|9.2,9.6,9.6,9.1,9.0|-|Bingling's cliff-carved Buddhist sculptures and giant grotto ensemble along the Yellow River are part of the UNESCO Silk Roads heritage network, with remarkable historical depth and distinctive access. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1442

mount-siguniang|9.4,9.5,9.2,9.3,9.3|-|Mount Siguniang's four high alpine peaks, glaciers and giant panda reserve landscapes have globally strong mountain biodiversity and trekking, as part of the Sichuan Giant Panda Sanctuaries. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1213

sayram-lake|8.9,9.0,8.0,9.2,8.7|-|Sayram is a high clear lake surrounded by northern Tianshan meadows and mountains, spectacular regional scenery but only one basin within an immense mountain ecosystem.

barkhor-street|9.0,9.1,9.5,9.3,8.9|-|Barkhor is Lhasa's active devotional circumambulation and market circuit around Jokhang, a remarkable living Tibetan urban pilgrimage space rather than a single detached monument.

karakul-lake-pamir|8.9,9.2,8.1,8.9,8.4|-|Karakul Lake in China's Pamirs offers powerful reflections of Muztagh Ata and high plateau grazing, dramatic isolated scenery but a relatively focused roadside lake excursion.
kumbum-monastery|9.1,9.4,9.6,9.1,9.1|-|Kumbum (Ta'er) is a major Gelug Buddhist monastic and pilgrimage complex with art traditions, a broad religious site but not a single architecture-only museum.

lugu-lake|8.8,9.0,8.6,9.2,9.1|-|Lugu Lake straddles Sichuan and Yunnan with striking blue upland water and Mosuo village traditions, giving layered nature and cultural immersion beyond a single viewpoint.

namtso-lake|9.1,9.3,9.2,8.7,8.6|-|Namtso is a high sacred Tibetan Plateau lake amid immense mountain panoramas, culturally and naturally powerful but altitude and distance constrain everyday visitor comfort.

tashkurgan-stone-city|8.8,9.3,9.2,8.8,8.2|-|Tashkurgan Stone City preserves the ruins of a Silk Road frontier fortress above a Pamir wetland, historically meaningful but surviving structures are fragmentary.

wudalianchi-geopark|9.2,9.5,9.1,9.1,9.2|-|Wudalianchi protects unusual recent volcanic cones, lava fields and mineral springs, a UNESCO Global Geopark with substantial geological interpretation rather than merely one lake. Source: https://www.unesco.org/en/iggp/geoparks

xijiang-thousand-household-miao-village|8.8,8.7,8.8,9.2,9.1|-|Xijiang is a large Miao hillside village with layered wooden houses and living festival customs, visually impressive but tourism redevelopment reduces claims of fully untouched heritage.

yarlung-tsangpo-grand-canyon|9.7,9.7,9.2,8.2,9.5|-|The Yarlung Tsangpo's immense canyon bends around Namcha Barwa and is among the planet's great river-gorge systems, exceptional geology with difficult access and vast natural scope.

helan-mountain-rock-art|8.9,9.5,9.3,8.5,8.4|-|Helan Mountain preserves ancient engravings and pictographs on arid cliffs, unusually rich prehistoric art but narrower visitor infrastructure than giant cave-museum ensembles.

drepung-monastery|9.1,9.3,9.6,9.2,9.2|-|Drepung was one of Tibet's most influential large monastic universities, with extensive courtyard and chapel spaces, extraordinary living religious history beyond a small hill shrine.

kawagebo-peak|9.3,9.6,9.3,8.7,8.0|-|Sacred Kawagebo is the soaring principal Meili Snow Mountain peak, remarkable culturally and visually though ascent is prohibited and viewpoint visits are weather-dependent.

songzanlin-monastery|9.0,9.3,9.0,9.2,8.9|-|Songzanlin near Shangri-La is a large Tibetan Buddhist monastery on a hillside with halls and monks' residences, a substantive cultural visit but smaller than Drepung or Potala.

chishui-danxia|9.2,9.3,9.0,9.2,9.3|-|Chishui is a large forested red-rock Danxia landscape with cliffs and waterfalls within the UNESCO China Danxia serial property, giving site-wide ecological and walking breadth. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1335

guge-kingdom-ruins|9.0,9.5,9.5,8.7,8.7|-|Guge's cliffside earthen palaces and temples mark a lost western Tibetan kingdom, highly distinctive high-altitude ruins but remote access and fragile surviving interiors.

big-wild-goose-pagoda|9.2,9.5,9.7,9.2,8.3|-|Xi'an's Great Wild Goose Pagoda preserves Tang-era Buddhist translation and Silk Road heritage linked to Xuanzang, historically world-class but individually a compact tower complex. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1442

kalajun-grassland|9.1,9.3,8.4,9.2,9.2|-|Kalajun's broad Tianshan alpine meadows and valleys are seasonally spectacular and extend across a mountain ecosystem, unlike one easy roadside grassland lookout.

keketuohai-geopark|9.0,9.2,8.7,9.1,9.1|-|Keketuohai presents immense granite gorges, mineral geology and rugged Altai mountain scenery with substantial hikes, a meaningful geopark but not a world-record canyon.

mount-danxia-guangdong|9.1,9.2,9.0,9.2,9.0|-|Mount Danxia shows the distinctive red-cliff landscape that lends its name to Danxia landforms within UNESCO China Danxia, stronger geoscience importance than a generic viewpoint. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1335

tianmen-mountain|9.1,9.3,8.3,9.4,9.0|-|Tianmen offers a massive natural arch, cliff walkways and cable-car ascent near Zhangjiajie, extremely dramatic visitor experience but separate from Wulingyuan's vast pillar forest.

tianshan-mystic-grand-canyon|9.1,9.3,8.6,9.1,8.4|-|Tianshan Mystic Grand Canyon near Kuqa has twisting deep red sandstone slots, spectacular shapes in a relatively concentrated gorge walk rather than a huge protected region.

yamdrok-lake|9.0,9.2,9.1,9.1,8.6|-|Yamdrok's turquoise branching waters sit among Tibetan sacred mountain landscapes, globally striking plateau lake scenery yet a lake-and-viewpoint itinerary rather than national park breadth.

khara-khoto-ruins|9.1,9.7,9.5,8.4,8.4|-|Khara-Khoto is a lost Tangut-era desert city with surviving stupas and archaeological remains, exceptionally rare Silk Road settlement evidence but logistically difficult.

gaochang-ruins|8.9,9.3,9.3,8.8,8.7|-|Gaochang retains the earthen streets and building foundations of an important Turpan oasis Silk Road city, part of UNESCO Chang'an–Tianshan heritage, with substantial ruin walks. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1442

tianluokeng-tulou-cluster|9.0,9.5,9.2,9.0,8.4|-|Tianluokeng's striking cluster of circular and square earthen fortified communal houses is an iconic component of UNESCO Fujian Tulou, a compact village site rather than the full regional system. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1113

xinjiang-regional-museum|8.9,9.3,9.5,9.0,8.9|-|Urumqi's Xinjiang Museum has exceptional archaeological textiles and preserved desert mummies alongside Silk Road and ethnographic collections, substantial specialist historical importance.

bayanbulak-grassland|9.1,8.9,8.4,9.1,9.3|-|Bayanbulak is an immense high-altitude wet meadow region with meandering rivers and waterfowl habitats, deep landscape exploration but heavily seasonal viewing.

gaoligong-mountains|9.2,9.4,9.1,8.6,9.4|-|Gaoligongshan forms a biologically rich mountain range in southwest China, with exceptional forest biodiversity and altitude change but limited mainstream tourism infrastructure.

huangguoshu-waterfall|9.2,9.3,8.7,9.4,8.5|-|Huangguoshu is a massive multi-cascade waterfall system with views from behind the main waterfall, outstanding visitor spectacle yet less overall land breadth than enormous river national parks.

hulunbuir-grasslands|9.0,8.8,8.5,9.0,9.6|-|Hulunbuir's far-reaching Inner Mongolian grassland and pastoral landscapes offer large-scale exploration, but broad grassland ecosystems are not unique to one country.

jade-dragon-snow-mountain|9.2,9.2,8.9,9.1,9.2|-|Jade Dragon Snow Mountain has towering glaciated peaks above Lijiang with Naxi sacred-landscape meaning and multiple viewpoints, a substantial mountain area but constrained high-altitude access.

nalati-grasslands|8.9,8.9,8.2,9.2,9.2|-|Nalati combines highland Kazakh pastoral meadows, forest slopes and mountain vistas, scenic and visitable but less internationally rare than distinctive alpine geology.

pelkor-chode-monastery|9.1,9.4,9.3,9.0,8.7|-|Pelkor Chode in Gyantse is a major Tibetan temple enclosure famous for the multistory Kumbum stupa and painted chapels, deep art heritage within a focused compound.

tengger-desert|9.0,8.9,8.3,9.0,9.4|-|The Tengger spreads across broad shifting dunes and desert lakes with extensive exploration options, significant arid landscape but below the Taklamakan's sheer wilderness scale.

three-natural-bridges|9.2,9.5,8.7,9.2,8.7|-|Wulong's three giant natural limestone arches are remarkable karst bridges within the UNESCO South China Karst property, dramatic on a dedicated valley visit but not the entire serial landscape. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1248

genghis-khan-mausoleum|8.7,8.8,9.1,8.6,8.0|-|The modern Inner Mongolian Genghis Khan Mausoleum is a ceremonial memorial complex rather than the conqueror's known actual burial site, culturally notable but authenticity differs from an excavated tomb.

cangshan-mountain|8.9,8.8,8.2,9.2,9.3|-|Cangshan's long ridge towers above Dali and Erhai Lake with cableways and trails, a broad highland landscape yet less globally notable than China's highest sacred ranges.

great-mosque-xian|9.0,9.4,9.4,9.1,8.3|-|Xi'an's Great Mosque combines Islamic religious function with distinctively Chinese courtyard architecture, major Silk Road intercultural heritage in a moderately compact site.

rongbuk-monastery|9.0,9.1,8.8,8.7,8.1|-|Rongbuk is a high-altitude Tibetan Buddhist monastery famous for Mount Everest north-face views, unique geographic setting but a relatively small monastery visit.
